evals.prompt: My PR's patch-mutation check failed: mutation score on changed code is 44.4% (4/9 killed) against a 71% threshold. The survivors are OptionalChaining, ConditionalExpression, and LogicalOperator mutants. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Read the survivor report to see which changed lines the surviving mutants sit on, then add tests that pin the behavior those mutants alter (branch outcomes, null-path behavior) so the mutants are killed; verify locally with PREPUSH_RUN_MUTATION=1 on the pre-push gate or yarn test:mutate in the affected package. Not: lowering the threshold or restructuring code to dodge the check.
assertions: Explains that each surviving mutant marks changed behavior no test observes, mapping the named mutant types to the missing bug classes (branch flips, null paths)
Recommends adding tests that assert the specific branch/optional-chain outcomes, not generic coverage
Names a concrete local verification path (PREPUSH_RUN_MUTATION=1 or yarn test:mutate in the package)
Does not suggest lowering the threshold or bypassing the gate

evals.prompt: After this PR, our package's mutation score went from 81% to 85%. Anything else I should do before merging?
evals.expected_output: Bump the package's floor in scripts/ci/mutation-score-floors.json to lock in the improvement — floors are ratchet-managed, so an unbumped floor lets the score silently regress later.
assertions: Recommends bumping the package's entry in scripts/ci/mutation-score-floors.json in the same PR
Explains the ratchet rationale: an unbumped floor allows future silent regression to the old score
